text.en: Teji wrote the names of her friends in a row. She counted the letters in each name, ticked the longest and crossed the shortest.

Let us do the name activity from the book. Write the names of some of your friends in a list.
First, count the letters in every name. Then tick the longest name and put a cross on the shortest name.
Next, look at the starting letter of your own name. Count how many names begin with the same letter.
Now find which starting letter is used the most. Count the names that begin with it.
You can also count the names that end with the same letter.
Last, write down the letters that are not the starting letter of any name in your list.
Boys and girls can compare too. Find the shortest and longest names among the boys, among the girls and in the whole class.
Sharing your method with the class is important. Different children can find the answer in different ways, and all of them can be right.

problem.en: Names: Anu, Ravi, Meena, Kiran. Which is longest and which is shortest?

text.en: Count the letters: Anu 3, Ravi 4, Meena 5, Kiran 5.
The most letters is 5, so Meena and Kiran are the longest names.

why.en: Two names can share the longest.

text.en: The fewest letters is 3, so Anu is the shortest.

why.en: The smallest count is the shortest name.

prompt.en: Can two names both be the longest name in a list? Explain.

requiredIdeas.en: Yes, if they have the same number of letters

commonMisconceptions.en: Only one name can be the longest

points.en: Count the letters to compare names.
Two names can have the same number of letters.
We can also compare the first and last letters of names.
